paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the Lord stays with you when the work gets hard. Paul got opposed and insulted in Corinth, and then the Lord spoke to him in a vision: "Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent." (Acts 18:9) That's not a pep talk from a stranger. The Lord gives a reason: "For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you, because I have many people in this city." (Acts 18:10)

Notice that the Lord doesn't only say "keep going." He tells Paul He has many people in that city (Acts 18:10), and Crispus and many Corinthians believed (Acts 18:8). So when the synagogue door closed on Paul (Acts 18:6), the work wasn't over. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer thinking my story was done, and the Lord had a whole bakery waiting.

And look at how Paul's year and a half in Corinth (Acts 18:11) ended up. Paul never got to speak at the judgment seat, and still Gallio drove the accusers away (Acts 18:14-16). Paul's job was to keep speaking, and the Lord had promised that no one would lay a hand on him (Acts 18:9-10). So keep showing up to the Word, baker, even when you feel worn down at the edges like I was.
